text:
maya (PM): quick sync — thinking about an autofallback policy UX that surfaces eligibility and a lightweight audit row. proposal: per-route toggle, 3 degrade modes (soft-queue, truncated-response, null-resp), and sampled decision traces. reactions? :thinking:

todd (eng): +1 to per-route. we need clear semantics for 'eligibility' tho. is it based on error codes, latency, model confidence, or all of the above?

sasha (sre): error+latency ORs are the simplest operationally. model confidence is noisy for some models. also: throttle windows matter — fallback during bursts vs persistent errors should differ.

kevin (design): UX note: show a one-line status on the route card: "Fallback: on · mode: soft-queue · sample: 2%" and a small "why" link that expands the decision logic. compactness is key.

maya (PM): agree. alexa, telemetry — what fields do we need in the trace to make audits useful but small?

alexa (telemetry): minimum: route, decision (allowed|blocked|fallbacked), trigger (500, timeout, high-latency, low-confidence), model_variant, timestamp, sample_id. size-wise aim for ~200 bytes per sampled decision. retention: 7d hot + 90d cold?

todd (eng): for implementation: propose policy shape like this (proto):

```
{
  "routes": ["/v1/chat","/v1/completions"],
  "eligibility": { "per_route": true, "min_model_score": 0.7, "on_error_codes": [500,502,504], "latency_ms_threshold": 1200 },
  "degrade_mode": "soft_queue", // soft_queue | truncated_response | null_response
  "audit_sampling": 0.02,
  "decision_ttl_hours": 72
}
```

kevin (design): UI question: when someone clicks "why" — show a short explanation and a link to the audit view for that sampled trace. avoid dumping raw JSON. show the trigger + riser graph snippet.

sasha (sre): also need an escape hatch: route-level manual "force fallback" and global emergency off switch. those should be visible in the console header when an incident is active.

maya (PM): good call. alexa — sampling rate default 2% ok? and can we provide an adaptive sampling that increases to, say, 20% during rollouts/incidents?

alexa (telemetry): yes. adaptive sample rules: increase based on error-rate delta or SLA breach. we can include a sample_ramp flag in the policy. storage costs will spike but only for short windows.

todd (eng): one more dev note: keep decision trace id stable across retries and caches so the audit can stitch requests. include kv cache hits.

kevin (design): think about microcopy for "degraded response" — be explicit to the app owner about fidelity impact. small tooltip: "Soft-queue delays token generation to allow stable model variant. Truncated-response shortens output for latency. Null-response returns fallback content."

maya (PM): sounds like we have a working spec. next steps: todd + alexa to prototype server-side traces, kevin to wire the small UI status row + "why" panel, sasha to draft the escape-hatch behavior. i'll schedule a 30m follow-up next week. :calendar:

deploy-bot: policy-canary v0.1 deployed to us-east-1 for internal routes at 2026-03-19T15:12:10Z :rocket:

sasha (sre): I'll run a short chaos test during the canary window and report traces to the audit view.

maya (PM): thanks all — please drop quick notes in the doc linked below when you start implementation: https://redwood.internal/notes/autofallback-spec
